title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Defense
description: Prevent SSRF attacks in microservices and cloud metadata endpoints.
precautions: Disallow direct user-controlled URLs in server-side fetches
Use allowlist for outbound targets and protocols
Block access to cloud metadata IPs (e.g., 169.254.169.254)
Normalize and validate URLs before requests
Route outbound via proxy with policy enforcement
steps: Introduce URL allowlist and scheme checks
Add egress firewall rules to block metadata endpoints

title: Command Injection Prevention
description: Avoid unsafe shell execution and injection via strict input handling.
precautions: Avoid shell invocation; prefer safe APIs
Never interpolate untrusted input into commands
Use fixed arguments and escape routines
steps: Refactor to library calls over shell
Use subprocess with explicit args, no shell=True

title: Insecure Deserialization Mitigation
description: Prevent arbitrary code execution via safe parsing and schema validation.
precautions: Use JSON with strict schema validation
Isolate parsing in sandbox if needed
steps: Add anomaly alerts on parser errors

title: Path Traversal Protection
description: Block directory traversal to sensitive paths in file handlers.
precautions: Normalize paths and enforce base directories
Map logical identifiers to storage (not raw paths)
Use OS permissions and chroot/jail where possible
Disable file serving from untrusted input

title: Clickjacking Defense
description: Protect UI from framing attacks using headers and CSP.
precautions: Implement UI anti-clickjacking overlays if needed
steps: Configure security headers in reverse proxy
Add functional tests for header enforcement

title: Open Redirect Prevention
precautions: Never trust redirect targets from user input
steps: Replace external URL redirects with route IDs
Write tests for malicious redirect inputs

title: Software Supply Chain Security
description: Secure dependencies and CI/CD pipeline integrity.
precautions: Isolate CI secrets and use short-lived tokens

title: Secrets Management Best Practices
description: Protect credentials using vaults and policy-based access control.
precautions: Use a secrets vault (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
Avoid storing secrets in code or configs
Scope secrets to minimal roles and TTLs
steps: Refactor applications to load secrets at runtime

title: Cloud Storage Exposure Prevention (S3/GCS)
description: Avoid public exposure and misconfigurations of object storage.
precautions: Disable public ACLs and enforce bucket policies
Encrypt objects at rest and in transit
Scan for PII and secrets in objects

title: Kubernetes Security Fundamentals
precautions: Use RBAC and namespaces for isolation
Scan images and enforce admission policies

title: LLM Prompt Injection and Data Exfiltration
description: Reduce prompt injection risks and unauthorized data leakage in LLM apps.
precautions: Isolate tool execution from raw model output
Restrict sensitive tool capabilities and scopes
steps: Introduce guardrails layer before tool calls
